say.2,952: two thousand, nine hundred and fifty-two

sentences.text: Who voted? Why did nobody say no? And who really runs China?
Not the public: just under 3,000 lawmakers.
But here's the weird part: this year, a billion people vote.
Every citizen from 18 can, but only for a local congress.
You back or reject each name, or write in someone else.
There are more names than seats, so some lose.
Now it gets strange: that's the only vote you get.
Each congress elects the one above: county, city, province, nation.
At the top, the National People's Congress passes the laws.
It meets for about a week a year.
It elects the president, with one name on the ballot.
In 2018, it scrapped his two-term limit.
He names the premier, who runs the government.
That's how Xi got a third term in 2023.
And the star above the pyramid? The Communist Party. Its top 205 members pick the real boss: Xi.
Is one name on a ballot a real choice?
